text:
leila: Quick flag while bringing Solstice-7B into our staging evals. License has a clause that might block on-device experiments. Paste below.

leila: ```
Section 5. Distribution and Deployment. The Model may be used for internal evaluation and hosted inference. You may not transfer, publish, or otherwise make the Model (including modified or quantized forms) available for download or execution on third-party or customer-controlled hardware without prior written authorization from the Model Provider. Attribution to the Provider and link to the model card is required on any public demonstration.
```

priya: Ugh. Does "make available for download or execution on third-party or customer-controlled hardware" cover us shipping a locked docker image with the quantized weights inside?

chris-legal: Short takeaway: yes, that's redistribution. A locked image still contains the artifacts needed to run offline. The phrase "including modified or quantized forms" is explicit.

tom: We're planning two things: (A) run 4-bit and 8-bit quant experiments on our infra, upload only benchmark logs; (B) offer a customer-facing air-gapped option in Dedicated where we hand over an appliance image. (B) is the problem.

chris-legal: Option summary:
- Internal evals + reports: allowed.
- Managed Dedicated (we host weights in customer VPC, never hand the raw files): probably allowed but depends on whether we physically transfer files to client infrastructure. If we retain custody and provide an access-controlled service, it's safer.
- Handing over images/weights: disallowed without explicit permission.

infra-bot: Recommend tagging model policy: `policy:staging-hosted-only` and blocking registry exports for models with "no-redistrib" license flag.

leila: Can we propose a limited sublicense to the Provider: distribute quantized artifacts only under a non-redistribution covenant + attribution + audit trail? That would enable our appliance customers.

chris-legal: Yes, request that. I can draft an email asking for: (1) permission to distribute quantized derivatives under a sublicense that forbids onward redistribution, (2) permission to embed weights in signed appliance images for named enterprise customers, (3) confirmation that pulling weights at install time from an access-controlled endpoint (with attestation) is permitted.

priya: From infra side: we can support an install-time pull model with attestation (image contacts our service, verifies entitlement, streams weights, then disk-encrypts them). That avoids directly handing files to customers. We should ask Provider if that meets their "no transfer" constraint.

pack-bot: Suggested temporary mitigation: `redwood model:set-policy solstice-7b hosted-only` and `model-registry:deny-export solstice-7b`.

tom: Bench notes: 4-bit QGlobal reduced memory by ~60% and gives 2.1x tokens/sec on our p4 cluster, quality drop ~3.5% on persona-turn evals. We'll keep results internal.

leila: I'll open T-5011 with the request and attach the eval artifacts. Chris, can you review the proposed email before I send?

chris-legal: Yep. I'll craft the ask and include three-tier proposals: evaluation-only, managed-hosting, and restricted redistribution (sublicense + attribution + audit). Also ask for sample clause language to permit signed runtime pulls.

priya: I'll add an ingress check to CI so no exportable artifacts are pushed to the public registry until we get clearance.

leila: Thanks. Action items: 1) set hosted-only + deny-export, 2) run internal quant benches and attach to T-5011, 3) legal outreach draft, 4) infra CI guard.

tom: :+1:

leila: Closing thread. Ping here or DM if Provider responds or infra needs help.
